chapter: Union, publishers, race and Harlem nightlife
title: Irving Mills's name on songs and credit for Ride Red Ride
summary: Publisher Irving Mills put his name on tunes in exchange for recording; JCH was uncredited on Ride Red Ride.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Jay C., what about companies like Irving Mills, the music publisher?
You can have them.
What was he like and who was he?

He's a big publisher. I got his name on a record back there. I haven't been paid for it, haven't collected for it. I will if I take time. Any record you record, just like when I was with Lucky Millinder's band, if you want to make a record you write a tune. This is your tune. So the leader says, O.K. Got your arrangement and everything? After the record is printed, you look on that record, you see by Irving Mills and so and so and so. I got a record back there to show it.
Irving Mills, you said that he would put his name on the song, every song. Would you get any money from it? About how much from each record?
I don't know. You get a percentage according to how the records sell.
Did he give you a contract?
Yeah, they give you a contract. About the only way you're going to get it recorded is you have to let him put his name on that.
Did you ever do anything for him?
I didn't get anything from him yet, but I am.
But do you have a contract, a document?
I have it now.
You got a piece of paper from him?
I'm not in no hurry. The longer I wait the more I get.
O.K., what about this? You said that he used to sign his name on - did he ever actually publish his music in sheet form?
No, I've never seen that in sheet form, not on a tune that I had written, but I have seen it on lots of others - "Written by Irving Mills"... Or Sidney Mills, one of the two.

Sometimes they used to do things like - Thelonious Monk's Around About Midnight has three names on it - Cootie Williams as a bandleader, the publisher, and Thelonious Monk. Would that also happen with Lucky Millinder, like say, would it appear "Lucky Millinder, Irving Mills, and Jay C. Higginbotham"? Would the band leader take it, a share of it?
I don't know about it. I don't remember but two names on records.
The reason why I asked you is because early you said that Lucky Millinder and Red Allen had taken some music from you.
'Ride Red Ride'. So the thing was that they didn't give you any credit whatsoever for it.
Not a quarter... And I couldn't do nothin'.
